units.source_text: 随着对柏木的深入了解，我才明白他讨厌永恒的美。

en.t: As I came to know Kashiwagi more deeply, I finally understood that he hated eternal beauty.

units.source_text: 他的嗜好仅限于瞬间消失的音乐或数日之间就枯萎的插花，他讨厌建筑和文学。

en.t: His tastes were confined to music that vanished in an instant or flower arrangements that withered within a few days; he hated architecture and literature.

units.source_text: 他所以到金阁，无疑也只是为了寻求明月照耀的瞬间的金阔而来的。

en.t: No doubt he had come to the Golden Pavilion only to seek the momentary Golden Pavilion illuminated by the bright moon.

units.source_text: 尽管如此，音乐的美是多么奇妙啊！

en.t: Even so, how wondrous the beauty of music is!

units.source_text: 吹奏者造就的这种短暂的美，宛如接螃似的短命的生物，生命本身完全是抽象的、创造的。

en.t: This fleeting beauty created by the player was like a short-lived creature, and life itself was wholly abstract and creative.

units.source_text: 没有比音乐更像生命的东西了，虽然同样是美，然而没有比金阁更远离生俞、更像污辱生的美了。

en.t: Nothing resembles life more than music; though both are forms of beauty, nothing is farther from life, or more like an insult to life, than the Golden Pavilion.

units.source_text: 柏木奏罢《源氏车》的瞬间，音乐这个架空的生命消逝了，可他那丑陋的肉体和阴郁的认识却丝毫没有损伤、没有改变，且依然存在那里。

en.t: The instant Kashiwagi finished playing “Genji-guruma,” the imaginary life called music vanished, yet his ugly body and gloomy awareness remained there, utterly unharmed and unchanged.
